modeled_state.date_basis: post-1956 restoration, checked against current NPS imagery
modeled_state.note: The National Register record says the wall logs were reset and the roof rebuilt. Do not present the model as an untouched 1888 fabric reconstruction.

must_have: Two separate rectangular saddle-V-notched log pens.
A 10 ft 2 in central breezeway that remains visibly open from east to west.
One continuous, shallow gable roof spanning both pens and the breezeway.
A sod-covered double-board roof with irregular natural edge and restrained thickness.
Horizontal log courses, visible chinking and projecting notched corner ends.
Openings placed from HABS sheets 2 through 4 rather than inferred from photographs.
must_not_have: A single solid rectangular cabin with the breezeway painted onto its facade.
A steep barn roof, gambrel roof, porch addition, chimney or modern glazing not shown by HABS/current NPS sources.
Closed doors, dark quads or alpha cards blocking the through-view.
Historic outbuildings reconstructed from foundation traces in this single-building candidate.

height_and_roof_pitch.note: Wall height is dimensioned 5 ft 6 in. Ridge height and pitch are scaled/derived from the measured elevation and remain explicitly uncertain.

spatial_layout.roof_ridge: continuous along the long axis over both pens and breezeway
spatial_layout.origin: center of the HABS overall wall envelope at grade
spatial_layout.terrain_contact: terrain-snap each corner conservatively; keep the cabin level and bury only an irregular 0.05-0.12 m footing band

construction.walls: Horizontal round/hewn logs with chinking; saddle-V-notched corners documented by NRHP/HABS.
construction.roof: Low common gable, double-board construction with sod cover; avoid a clean modern turf slab.
construction.floor_and_foundation: Exterior grade contact and sparse historic foundation evidence only; do not invent a continuous modern concrete foundation.
construction.breezeway: True open volume. Interior side walls, ground, roof underside and through-view receive normal game lighting and depth.
construction.openings: Trace dimensions and offsets directly from the registered HABS floor plan/elevations. Treat the sheet-2 note that one breezeway log wall appears to be a later addition as uncertain interior detail and omit it unless present-day photographs confirm it.

materials.log_and_chinking: One compact, evenly lit tileable atlas family with restrained color variation and no landscape or baked sunlight.
materials.sod_roof: Shader-compatible muted soil/grass material, sparse at edges; no high-density grass geometry outside LOD0.
materials.boards_and_openings: Share one dark weathered-board material; actual voids and recess depth remain geometry.

geometry_policy.lod0: Spend geometry on the open dogtrot, roof edge, log-end silhouette and shallow opening depth; batch repeated logs/materials.
geometry_policy.lod1: Replace log relief with baked/material detail but retain separate pens and open breezeway.
geometry_policy.lod2: Use a minimal two-material silhouette with a real central void; never collapse to a solid box.

acceptance_checks: Measured overall plan is 12.624 m long and each pen is approximately 4.8 m deep.
The clear breezeway is 3.099 m wide and remains open in all LODs.
The HABS-derived model fits within the mapped 13.1 m by 5.3 m upstream footprint/roof envelope after overhang is accounted for.
Close east and west captures show real parallax and terrain through the breezeway.
South/north gable silhouette, eaves, wall height and roof pitch match registered HABS elevations.
No geometry represents undocumented vanished ranch buildings.
